Positional Interdependence introduces a dependency kernel that captures how roles interact dynamically. Institutional Affiliation Graph extends this to a network model where institutions act as hubs influencing player movement and role evolution. These operators form a dualistic system: one layer encodes static role assignments, while another encodes dynamic interdependencies. Failure modes occur when institutional constraints break down or when positional dependencies exceed team capacity. The system exhibits a duality between discrete role assignment and continuous interdependence, enabling both Bayesian inference and state-transition modeling.
